patterns: is it the same as computing
entries.answer: Information technology is the use of computers and networks to store, move and process information, and the field is broader than computing in the narrow sense of programming. What separates it is usually the systems side: hardware, networking, security and support rather than only software being written. That is why an IT course often contains little code, and why someone who can program but cannot run a network is not automatically employable in the field.

patterns: is help desk an it job
what does a help desk do
entries.answer: A help desk is the front line of technical support, where users report problems and someone either resolves or escalates them. It is the role most people picture when they say they work in IT, and it is mostly problem-solving under time pressure rather than building anything. The measure of the job is what proportion of tickets are closed without escalating, and the skill that matters most is asking the user the right question before touching anything.

patterns: what is the internet layer model
entries.answer: Networking is the practice of connecting computers so they can share data and resources, and it covers everything from a cable between two machines to the routing between organisations. The model underneath is layered, with each layer handling its own job and passing upwards, which is why a fault at one level looks like a failure at another. A useful mental model is that the network moves packets and does not care what is inside them, which is exactly why it cannot tell a valid request from a forged one.

patterns: what does a cybersecurity person do
entries.answer: Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting systems and data from unauthorised access and from being changed or destroyed. Most of the work is prevention and detection, since the cheapest fix is not being compromised at all. The part outsiders underrate is that technology is the smaller half, and that patching, access control and backups prevent far more incidents than any security product.

patterns: is it support an easy job
what does an it support person do
entries.answer: IT support is the work of keeping someone's technology working, and it splits into desktop support for the person in front of you and infrastructure work behind the scenes. Most entry-level roles are the first kind, which is a service job with technical content rather than a purely technical one. The skills that decide how well somebody does are communication and the discipline to ask before acting, and neither of them is taught by the technical content.
